Conversation, family & daily routines

like verb

find pleasing

also I like this, I like it, do you like it?, I like to, I like doing, I don’t like

classical

Ter. Ad. 911: Placet, pater lepidissime.
Cic. Att. 2.4.1: mihi maximē placet
Traupman p. 102: hoc mihi placet

placet (mihi)

impersonal: the thing liked is the subject, the person in the dative

I like it, it pleases me

English “I like this” turns round: hoc mihi placet, “this pleases me”. “Do you like it?”: placetne tibi?.

Other words

  • juvat (mē) — I like to, I enjoy (doing)

    impersonal, with the person in the accusative and an infinitive · also used · classical · Hor. S. 2.6.32: hoc juvat et mellī est; Traupman p. 102: mē juvat hoc facere

    For liking to do something: mē juvat hoc facere, I like doing this (see enjoy).

Examples

  • Mē juvat hoc facere.

    I like to do this.Traupman p. 102

See also enjoy, favourite, love, want.

SourcesLewis & Short: placeo · Lewis & Short: juvo
